question.text: In a bull call spread, the maximum loss equals:

answer.text: The net premium paid (lower strike call premium minus higher strike call premium received)
The difference between the two strike prices

explanation.text: The Logic: Bull call spread = long the lower-strike call and short the higher-strike call, creating an initial net cash outflow. Maximum loss = net premium paid = premium paid for lower call - premium received for higher call (e.g., 0.10 - 0.04 = 0.06). This loss is realised when USDINR stays at or below the lower strike at expiry. The Trap: Max loss is NOT the full premium of the lower call — it's reduced by the premium received from selling the higher call. Note: The reduced cost (vs a naked long call) is the main advantage of the bull call spread. Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.101-103.
